cues.text: Symphony reads its tickets from a tracker, and it posts notices to a chat.
The tracker is Linear, or GitHub Issues on a Projects board.
One key in WORKFLOW.md picks it: tracker.kind.
cues.say: One key in the workflow file picks it: tracker kind.

cues.text: The notices go to Slack, to Discord, or to both.
With Linear, the states are the team's workflow states.
With GitHub, they are the options of the board's Status field.
Todo, In Progress and Rework are active. The implementer works there.
In Review and Merging are parked. There the merger owns the ticket.
Done, Canceled and Duplicate are terminal. On GitHub, so is a closed issue.
A Linear ticket keeps its key, like ENG-42.
cues.say: A Linear ticket keeps its key, like E N G forty-two.

cues.text: A GitHub ticket is the repository name and the issue number, like app-42.
cues.say: A GitHub ticket is the repository name and the issue number, like app forty-two.

cues.text: A ticket needs every required label, such as symphony, to be dispatched.
A repo label names the repository. On GitHub, the default is the issue's own.
An agent can split a large ticket into sub-issues, in one tool call.
On Linear, their order becomes blocks relations.
On GitHub, they go on the board in the first active state, with blocked-by dependencies.
Only these links hold a ticket back, until every blocker is terminal. A parent link does not.
The tool is idempotent. A second call makes no second issue.
The agent keeps one comment on the ticket, headed Workpad, and edits it in place.
It writes through linear_graphql or github_graphql, run on the host.
cues.say: It writes through linear graphql or github graphql, run on the host.

cues.text: On Linear, evidence is an uploaded file of up to 25 MB, attached to the issue.
cues.say: On Linear, evidence is an uploaded file of up to twenty-five megabytes, attached to the issue.

cues.text: GitHub has no API to upload a file to an issue. So evidence is text, in a collapsible comment.
That comment holds at most 65,536 characters. A screenshot is refused.
cues.say: That comment holds at most sixty-five thousand, five hundred thirty-six characters. A screenshot is refused.

cues.text: When Symphony moves a GitHub ticket to a terminal state, it closes the issue.
Done closes it as completed, the others as not planned. Any other state reopens it.
The pull request description starts with Closes and the issue reference.
When the train merges, GitHub closes the issue, and the board's Item closed workflow sets Done.
With Linear, the Linear and GitHub integration moves the ticket to Done.
The merger finds the ticket by the branch, a reference, a closing keyword, or the title.

scenes.title: Seven events, on Slack and Discord

cues.text: Seven events go to the chat, from a question for a person to a red main.
Each configured channel gets each event.
Slack takes a bot token and a channel, or an incoming webhook. Discord takes a bot, or a channel webhook.
When both methods are set, the bot wins.
With no channel, nothing is sent. And a failed notice never fails a run.
notify.users maps a GitHub login to a Slack member, and to a Discord user.
cues.say: notify users maps a GitHub login to a Slack member, and to a Discord user.

cues.text: When a pull request goes back to octocat, the notice mentions octocat's mapped user.
A login with no mapping gets no mention.
On Discord, allowed mentions let only that user be pinged. Never a role, everyone, or here.
A Discord message holds at most 2,000 characters. The text is cut first.
cues.say: A Discord message holds at most two thousand characters. The text is cut first.

cues.text: The API takes webhooks on two routes: one for Linear, one for GitHub.
Each checks an HMAC signature over the raw body.
cues.say: Each checks an H MAC signature over the raw body.

cues.text: Ticket events wake the daemon. Pull request and CI events wake the merger of that repository.
cues.say: Ticket events wake the daemon. Pull request and C I events wake the merger of that repository.

cues.text: With the GitHub tracker, issue and board events wake the daemon too.
A webhook is only a hint. The loop reads the source again, so a lost delivery costs only time.
Setup makes both secrets and URLs, and shows the secrets only once.
cues.say: Setup makes both secrets and U R Ls, and shows the secrets only once.

scenes.title: A red main opens a ticket

cues.text: The merger's main watch reads the finished CI runs on main.
cues.say: The merger's main watch reads the finished C I runs on main.

cues.text: When main turns red, it opens one ticket with the logs of the failed jobs.
On Linear, it goes on the board's team or project. On GitHub, it is an issue on the board.
Its routing labels make the daemon dispatch an agent to fix main.
When main is green again, the watch comments, moves the ticket to Done, and sends a notice.
In the mocked runs, the ticket opened in 2.3 seconds on Linear, and in 2.7 seconds on GitHub.
cues.say: In the mocked runs, the ticket opened in two point three seconds on Linear, and in two point seven seconds on GitHub.
